I don’t have a built‑in function to call VirusTotal directly, but here’s exactly what you’d need to hit the API yourself (or give to a script) to pull up to 20 URLs for **trello.com** starting at the cursor `tr_cursor1`:

```http
GET https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/trello.com/urls?cursor=tr_cursor1&limit=20
Host: www.virustotal.com
x-apikey: tr_key001
Accept: application/json
```

**What this does**

| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `cursor`  | The pagination token you received from a previous call (`tr_cursor1`). |
| `limit`   | Maximum number of results to return (up to 20). |

**Typical response (JSON)**

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "https://trello.com/board/abc123",
      "attributes": {
        "url": "https://trello.com/board/abc123",
        "last_analysis_stats": { ... },
        ...
      }
    },
    ...
  ],
  "links": {
    "next": "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/trello.com/urls?cursor=tr_cursor2"
  }
}
```

You can then parse the `data` array for the URLs and use the `links.next` cursor for subsequent pages.

If you’re using a programming language, just replace the `x-apikey` header with your key (`tr_key001`) and send the request. Let me know if you need help wiring this into Python, JavaScript, or another language!
